questions.questionTextEn: Peroxomonosulfuric acid (Caro's acid, $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_5$) contains
optionsEn: sulfur in the $+8$ oxidation state with no $\text{O}-\text{O}$ bond
sulfur in the $+6$ oxidation state and one peroxo ($-\text{O}-\text{O}-$) linkage
sulfur in the $+4$ oxidation state and two peroxo linkages
sulfur in the $+6$ oxidation state and one $\text{S}-\text{H}$ bond
questions.explanationEn: Caro's acid has the structure $\text{HO}-\text{SO}_2-\text{O}-\text{O}-\text{H}$. Because two oxygen atoms form a peroxo ($-\text{O}-\text{O}-$) linkage (oxidation state $-1$ each) and three are normal oxygens ($-2$ each), sulfur is in its maximum oxidation state of $+6$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The deep blue color and paramagnetism of a dilute solution of sodium metal in liquid ammonia are primarily due to the presence of
optionsEn: ammoniated sodium cations $[\text{Na}(\text{NH}_3)_x]^+$
ammoniated (solvated) electrons $[e(\text{NH}_3)_y]^-$
sodium amide ($\text{NaNH}_2$)
dissolved $\text{Na}_2$ dimers
questions.explanationEn: Alkali metals dissolve in liquid $\text{NH}_3$ to produce ammoniated cations and solvated electrons: $\text{Na} + (x+y)\text{NH}_3 \to [\text{Na}(\text{NH}_3)_x]^+ + [e(\text{NH}_3)_y]^-$. The solvated electrons absorb in the red/near-IR region (imparting a deep blue color) and are unpaired (making the dilute solution paramagnetic).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The correct decreasing order of ionic radii among the isoelectronic species $\text{N}^{3-}$, $\text{O}^{2-}$, $\text{F}^-$, $\text{Na}^+$, and $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ is
optionsEn: $\text{Mg}^{2+} > \text{Na}^+ > \text{F}^- > \text{O}^{2-} > \text{N}^{3-}$
$\text{N}^{3-} > \text{O}^{2-} > \text{F}^- > \text{Na}^+ > \text{Mg}^{2+}$
$\text{F}^- > \text{O}^{2-} > \text{N}^{3-} > \text{Na}^+ > \text{Mg}^{2+}$
$\text{N}^{3-} > \text{F}^- > \text{O}^{2-} > \text{Mg}^{2+} > \text{Na}^+$
questions.explanationEn: All five ions have $10$ electrons ($1s^2 2s^2 2p^6$). As the nuclear charge $Z$ increases from $\text{N}^{3-}$ ($Z=7$) to $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ ($Z=12$), the effective nuclear charge $Z_{\text{eff}}$ increases and pulls the electron cloud closer to the nucleus. Hence, ionic radius decreases in the order $\text{N}^{3-} > \text{O}^{2-} > \text{F}^- > \text{Na}^+ > \text{Mg}^{2+}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Although $\text{Cu}^+$ ($96\text{ pm}$) and $\text{Na}^+$ ($102\text{ pm}$) have nearly identical ionic radii and the same charge, $\text{CuCl}$ has a much lower melting point and much lower water solubility than $\text{NaCl}$ because
optionsEn: $\text{Cu}^+$ has a pseudo-noble gas $3d^{10}$ configuration that poorly shields the nuclear charge, giving higher polarizing power
$\text{Na}^+$ has a higher effective nuclear charge than $\text{Cu}^+$
$\text{CuCl}$ has a higher Madelung constant than $\text{NaCl}$
$\text{Cu}^+$ forms stronger hydrogen bonds with chloride ions
questions.explanationEn: By Fajan's rules, cations with an $18$-electron pseudo-noble gas core ($\text{Cu}^+$: $[\text{Ar}]3d^{10}$) experience poor shielding by $d$-electrons compared to an $8$-electron noble gas core ($\text{Na}^+$: $[\text{Ne}]$). Hence $\text{Cu}^+$ strongly polarizes $\text{Cl}^-$, imparting substantial covalent character to $\text{CuCl}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The experimental gas-phase dipole moment of $\text{NH}_3$ ($1.47\text{ D}$) is significantly larger than that of $\text{NF}_3$ ($0.24\text{ D}$) primarily because
optionsEn: $\text{NF}_3$ is trigonal planar whereas $\text{NH}_3$ is trigonal pyramidal
in $\text{NH}_3$ the lone-pair orbital dipole reinforces the resultant $\text{N}-\text{H}$ bond dipoles, whereas in $\text{NF}_3$ it opposes the resultant $\text{N}-\text{F}$ bond dipoles
$\text{N}-\text{H}$ bonds are more polar than $\text{N}-\text{F}$ bonds
$\text{NF}_3$ lacks a lone pair on nitrogen
questions.explanationEn: Both $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{NF}_3$ are trigonal pyramidal. In $\text{NH}_3$, $\chi_{\text{N}} > \chi_{\text{H}}$, so the three $\text{N}-\text{H}$ bond dipoles point toward $\text{N}$ and reinforce the lone-pair dipole. In $\text{NF}_3$, $\chi_{\text{F}} > \chi_{\text{N}}$, so the three $\text{N}-\text{F}$ bond dipoles point away from $\text{N}$ and largely cancel the lone-pair dipole.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: At room temperature, the $^{19}\text{F}$ NMR spectrum of gaseous $\text{PF}_5$ exhibits only a single doublet (coupled to $^{31}\text{P}$) instead of two separate signals for axial and equatorial fluorines. The reason for this observation is
optionsEn: $\text{PF}_5$ adopts a pentagonal planar structure in the gas phase
rapid intramolecular exchange of axial and equatorial fluorines via Berry pseudorotation through a square pyramidal ($C_{4v}$) transition state
rapid intermolecular $\text{F}^-$ dissociation in the gas phase
accidental chemical shift equivalence of axial and equatorial $^{19}\text{F}$ nuclei
questions.explanationEn: $\text{PF}_5$ is fluxional at room temperature: axial and equatorial fluorines rapidly interconvert on the NMR timescale via **Berry pseudorotation** passing through a low-barrier square pyramidal ($C_{4v}$) transition state, averaging the two environments into one $^{19}\text{F}$ doublet (due to $^1J_{\text{P-F}}$ coupling).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The silicate anionic repeat units $[(\text{Si}_4\text{O}_{11})^{6-}]_n$ and $[(\text{Si}_2\text{O}_5)^{2-}]_n$ correspond, respectively, to
optionsEn: sheet silicates (phyllosilicates) and double-chain silicates (amphiboles)
double-chain silicates (amphiboles) and sheet silicates (phyllosilicates)
cyclic silicates and 3D framework silicates (tectosilicates)
pyrosilicates and single-chain silicates (pyroxenes)
questions.explanationEn: Double-chain silicates (amphiboles, such as asbestos) have alternating tetrahedra sharing $2$ and $3$ oxygens, yielding $[(\text{Si}_4\text{O}_{11})^{6-}]_n$. Sheet silicates (phyllosilicates, such as mica and talc) have every $\text{SiO}_4$ tetrahedron sharing $3$ oxygens in a 2D plane, yielding $[(\text{Si}_2\text{O}_5)^{2-}]_n$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Reaction of diborane ($\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$) with two equivalents of trimethylamine ($\text{NMe}_3$) and with two equivalents of ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$) at low temperature yields, respectively,
optionsEn: $2\,\text{H}_3\text{B}\cdot\text{NMe}_3$ (symmetrical cleavage) and $[\text{BH}_2(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+[\text{BH}_4]^-$ (unsymmetrical cleavage)
$[\text{BH}_2(\text{NMe}_3)_2]^+[\text{BH}_4]^-$ (unsymmetrical cleavage) and $2\,\text{H}_3\text{B}\cdot\text{NH}_3$ (symmetrical cleavage)
$2\,\text{H}_3\text{B}\cdot\text{NMe}_3$ and $2\,\text{H}_3\text{B}\cdot\text{NH}_3$ (both symmetrical cleavage)
$\text{B}_3\text{N}_3\text{Me}_6$ and $\text{B}_3\text{N}_3\text{H}_6$
questions.explanationEn: Bulky Lewis bases such as $\text{NMe}_3$, $\text{CO}$, and $\text{THF}$ cause **symmetrical cleavage** of $\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$ to give $2\,\text{H}_3\text{B}\cdot\text{NMe}_3$. Small, hard bases like $\text{NH}_3$ cause **unsymmetrical cleavage** at low temperature to yield the ionic diammoniate of diborane, $[\text{BH}_2(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+[\text{BH}_4]^-$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The $\text{H}-\text{E}-\text{H}$ bond angles in $\text{NH}_3$, $\text{PH}_3$, $\text{AsH}_3$, and $\text{SbH}_3$ are $107.8^\circ$, $93.5^\circ$, $91.8^\circ$, and $91.3^\circ$, respectively. The sharp drop from $\text{NH}_3$ to $\text{PH}_3$ is best explained by
optionsEn: increased steric repulsion between $\text{H}$ atoms in $\text{PH}_3$
Drago's rule: minimal $s\text{--}p$ hybridization in heavier pnictogen hydrides, so bonding uses nearly pure $p$-orbitals while the lone pair remains in a predominantly $s$-orbital
$d$-orbital participation in $\text{PH}_3$ forming $sp^3d$ hybrids
stronger $\text{P}-\text{H}$ hydrogen bonding in the gas phase
questions.explanationEn: For heavier main-group elements ($n \ge 3$) bonded to low-electronegativity atoms like $\text{H}$ (Drago's rule), the $ns\text{--}np$ energy gap and larger atomic radius make $s\text{--}p$ hybridization energetically unfavorable. Bonding occurs via nearly pure orthogonal $p$-orbitals ($\sim 90^\circ$), with the lone pair residing mostly in the $ns$ orbital.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In an Ellingham diagram for metal oxides, the $\text{Mg}/\text{MgO}$ line lies below the $\text{Al}/\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ line below $\sim 1350\,^\circ\text{C}$ and crosses above it above $\sim 1350\,^\circ\text{C}$ (due to the boiling of $\text{Mg}$ at $1090\,^\circ\text{C}$). Consequently,
optionsEn: $\text{Mg}$ can reduce $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ below $1350\,^\circ\text{C}$, whereas $\text{Al}$ can reduce $\text{MgO}$ above $1350\,^\circ\text{C}$
$\text{Al}$ can reduce $\text{MgO}$ at all temperatures
$\text{Mg}$ can reduce $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ at all temperatures
neither metal can reduce the other's oxide at any temperature
questions.explanationEn: In an Ellingham diagram, the metal whose oxide line lies **lower** (more negative $\Delta_f G^\circ$) can thermodynamically reduce the oxide of a metal whose line lies **higher**. Because $\text{Mg}$ boils at $1090\,^\circ\text{C}$, its $\Delta_f G^\circ$ line bends sharply upward and crosses above $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ around $1350\,^\circ\text{C}$. Thus $\text{Mg}$ reduces $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ below $1350\,^\circ\text{C}$, and $\text{Al}$ reduces $\text{MgO}$ above $1350\,^\circ\text{C}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) based on VSEPR theory and Bent's rule is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: In $\text{SF}_4$, the lone pair occupies an equatorial position and the axial $\text{S}-\text{F}$ bonds are longer than the equatorial $\text{S}-\text{F}$ bonds.
In $\text{PCl}_2\text{F}_3$, two $\text{F}$ atoms occupy axial sites while one $\text{F}$ and two $\text{Cl}$ atoms occupy equatorial sites.
In $\text{ClF}_3$, the axial $\angle\text{F}_{\text{ax}}-\text{Cl}-\text{F}_{\text{ax}}$ angle is slightly less than $180^\circ$ due to lone-pair repulsion.
In $\text{XeF}_4$, the two lone pairs occupy adjacent (*cis*) positions in the octahedron.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A) True: Equatorial placement minimizes $90^\circ$ lone pair–bond pair repulsions; axial $pd$ bonds are longer than equatorial $sp^2$ bonds.
- (B) True: By Bent's rule, electronegative $\text{F}$ preferentially fills both axial sites first, with the third $\text{F}$ going equatorial.
- (C) True: Two equatorial lone pairs push the axial $\text{F}$ atoms slightly toward the equatorial $\text{F}$ ($\angle\text{F}_{\text{ax}}-\text{Cl}-\text{F}_{\text{ax}} \approx 175^\circ$).
- (D) False: In $\text{XeF}_4$, the two lone pairs occupy opposite (*trans*) positions, giving square planar geometry.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the froth floatation process used for concentrating sulfide ores, which of the following statement(s) is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: Collectors such as pine oil or potassium ethyl xanthate enhance the non-wettability (hydrophobicity) of the mineral particles.
Froth stabilizers such as cresols or aniline stabilize the air-bubble froth.
In a mixed ore of $\text{ZnS}$ and $\text{PbS}$, $\text{NaCN}$ acts as a depressant that selectively prevents $\text{ZnS}$ from entering the froth by forming soluble $\text{Na}_2[\text{Zn(CN)}_4]$.
Oxide ores like haematite ($\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$) are preferentially concentrated by froth floatation over sulfide ores.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A), (B), (C) are all standard principles of froth floatation.
- (D) False: Froth floatation is specifically suited to sulfide ores; haematite is concentrated by gravity/magnetic separation.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) regarding ionization enthalpy and electron gain enthalpy is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: The second ionization enthalpy of $\text{O}$ is higher than that of $\text{F}$.
The first electron gain enthalpy of $\text{S}$ is more negative than that of $\text{O}$.
The second electron gain enthalpy of $\text{O}$ ($\text{O}^-(g) + e^- \to \text{O}^{2-}(g)$) is endothermic.
The first ionization enthalpy of $\text{Mg}$ is lower than that of $\text{Al}$.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A) True: $\text{O}^+$ has a half-filled $2p^3$ configuration, giving $\text{IE}_2(\text{O}) > \text{IE}_2(\text{F})$ ($2p^4$).
- (B) True: $\text{O}$ suffers strong $2p$ interelectronic repulsion, so $\Delta_{\text{eg}} H(\text{S}) = -200\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ is more negative than $\Delta_{\text{eg}} H(\text{O}) = -141\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
- (C) True: Adding an electron to negatively charged $\text{O}^-$ requires overcoming electrostatic repulsion ($\Delta_{\text{eg}} H_2 > 0$, endothermic).
- (D) False: $\text{Mg}$ ($3s^2$) has higher $\text{IE}_1$ than $\text{Al}$ ($3s^2 3p^1$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) regarding xenon compounds is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: $\text{XeO}_3$ is trigonal pyramidal ($C_{3v}$) with one lone pair on xenon.
$\text{XeO}_4$ is tetrahedral ($T_d$) with zero lone pairs on xenon.
In the gas phase, $\text{XeF}_6$ adopts a distorted octahedral (capped octahedral) structure due to a stereochemically active lone pair.
$\text{XeF}_2$ is bent with an $\angle\text{F}-\text{Xe}-\text{F}$ angle of $104.5^\circ$.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A) True: $\text{XeO}_3$ has $3$ $\text{Xe}=\text{O}$ bonds and $1$ lone pair ($\text{SN}=4$, trigonal pyramidal).
- (B) True: $\text{XeO}_4$ has $4$ $\text{Xe}=\text{O}$ bonds and $0$ lone pairs ($\text{SN}=4$, tetrahedral).
- (C) True: $\text{XeF}_6$ ($6$ bond pairs + $1$ lone pair, $\text{SN}=7$) is a fluxional distorted octahedron in the gas phase.
- (D) False: $\text{XeF}_2$ ($2$ bond pairs + $3$ equatorial lone pairs) is strictly linear ($180^\circ$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of direct $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds present in one molecule of hypophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Hypophosphorous acid has the tetrahedral structure $\text{H}_2\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})$, containing $1$ $\text{P}=\text{O}$ bond, $1$ $\text{P}-\text{OH}$ bond, and $2$ direct $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of terminal $\text{P}=\text{O}$ bonds in one molecule of phosphorus pentoxide ($\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: In the adamantane-like cage of $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$, $6$ oxygens form $\text{P}-\text{O}-\text{P}$ bridges along the six edges of the $\text{P}_4$ tetrahedron, and the remaining $4$ oxygens form terminal $\text{P}=\text{O}$ bonds (one on each phosphorus atom).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of terminal $\text{S}=\text{O}$ double bonds present in one molecule of peroxodisulfuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_8$) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Peroxodisulfuric acid has the structure $\text{HO}-\text{SO}_2-\text{O}-\text{O}-\text{SO}_2-\text{OH}$. Each sulfur atom carries two terminal $\text{S}=\text{O}$ bonds, giving a total of $4$ terminal $\text{S}=\text{O}$ bonds.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn:
The gas-phase dipole moment of $\text{HCl}$ is $1.08\text{ D}$ and its internuclear bond length is $127.5\text{ pm}$. The percentage ionic character of the $\text{H}-\text{Cl}$ bond is _______ $\%$. *(round off to one decimal place)*

[Given: $1\text{ D} = 3.336 \times 10^{-30}\text{ C m}$; elementary charge $e = 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$]
questions.explanationEn:
For $100\%$ ionic character, $\mu_{\text{ionic}} = e \cdot d = (1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C})(127.5 \times 10^{-12}\text{ m}) = 2.04255 \times 10^{-29}\text{ C m}$.
The observed dipole moment is $\mu_{\text{obs}} = 1.08 \times 3.336 \times 10^{-30} = 3.60288 \times 10^{-30}\text{ C m}$.
Percentage ionic character $= \frac{3.60288 \times 10^{-30}}{2.04255 \times 10^{-29}} \times 100\% = 17.64\% \approx 17.6\%$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Inorganic Chemistry I: Periodicity, Chemical Bonding, Main Group & Metallurgy (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: According to Molecular Orbital Theory, the bond order of the dioxygenyl cation $\text{O}_2^+$ is _______. *(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn:
$\text{O}_2^+$ has $11$ valence electrons: $(\sigma_{2s})^2(\sigma^*_{2s})^2(\sigma_{2p_z})^2(\pi_{2p})^4(\pi^*_{2p})^1$.
Thus $N_b = 8$ and $N_a = 3$, giving $\text{BO} = \frac{8 - 3}{2} = 2.5$.

questions.questionTextEn: Using Slater's rules for a neutral copper atom ($Z = 29$, ground-state configuration $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^{10} 4s^1$), the difference $Z_{\text{eff}}(3d) - Z_{\text{eff}}(4s)$ is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
